newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss can't confirm Tajik hostage shooting.
newsitem.headline: Swiss can't confirm Tajik hostage shooting.

text.p: The Swiss defence ministry said on Thursday it had no confirmation of the reported killing of a U.N. military observer in Tajikistan by rebels holding more than a dozen Russian and Western hostages, including two Swiss.

Spokesman Urs Peter Stebler expressed caution about the report by Russia's Itar-Tass news agency and said Swiss contacts with the United Nations in New York and the Tajik capital Dushanbe had not confirmed the incident.
"For us, this report is not credible," he told Reuters. "We are continuing to seek information from the Tajik government and the United Nations in New York but for the time being, we have nothing."

An Itar-Tass correspondent, herself one of the hostages who are being held near Obigarm, 80 km (50 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe, reported the shooting of the U.N. military observer by satellite phone to her office in Moscow.

The Tajik government earlier on Thursday flew in 40 rebels from Afghanistan ahead of a deadline set by the rebel group holding the hostages but their release was delayed by haggling over details, officials said.
Another hostage working for Interfax news agency also telephoned from Tajikistan to confirm the shooting.

The hostages include four U.N. military observers, four Russian reporters and four workers with the U.N. refugee agency. The rebels also seized Tajikistan's security minister on Saturday when he flew in to negotiate the captives' release.
